name: Huai'an Local Disaster Recovery Center
developer: Huai'an Municipal Big Data Management Center
notes: Municipal development and reform approval for a new local disaster recovery center in Huai'an using leased cabinet resources plus servers, switching, security, backup appliance and disaster recovery platform equipment.

name: Huai'an Cloud Platform Expansion Project
developer: Huai'an Municipal Big Data Management Center
notes: Expansion of city government cloud infrastructure at Huai'an Zhiyouwo Digital Technology Industrial Park and the municipal administrative center equipment room; includes leased cabinet and machine-room services, servers, storage, network, backup and cloud-platform software.

name: Huaiyin Public Security Data Center Machine Room Construction Project
developer: Huai'an Public Security Bureau Huaiyin Branch
notes: Government procurement and contract records for a data-center computer room build, covering decoration, electrical, UPS, grounding, cold aisle, fresh air, structured cabling, security, monitoring and fire-suppression systems; contract value RMB 5.851 million.

name: Lianyungang Wukong Intelligent Computing Center
developer: Lianyungang Haizhou District / local digital company
notes: Xinhua reported launch of the 1600P computing center and operator-resource interconnection in May 2024; later local reporting described Wukong as an industrial intelligent-computing node with roughly 6500P to 6876P of computing resources.

name: Lianyungang City Big Data Center
developer: Lianyungang Municipal Government / H3C and partners
notes: H3C case study says the city big data center is about 45,000 sqm, can accommodate 5,000 cabinets, hosts the Lianyungang government cloud platform and base databases, and had aggregated data from 65 municipal units and 138 systems.

name: Lianyun New City Mobile Cloud Computing Center
developer: China Mobile Jiangsu / Lianyungang Lianyun District
notes: Lianyun District reports deployed computing infrastructure in the Belt and Road Big Data Industrial Park; official response says the mobile big data center passed CQC A-level room, ISO20000/27001 and MLPS level-3 certification and had 697 computing cabinets in production.

name: China Telecom Lianyungang Tianyi Cloud Center
notes: District government article says the cloud center in Lianyun New City occupied 47.53 mu and first phase had 232 cabinets; city data bureau response says telecom big data center basic supporting facilities were complete with 232 sale-ready 6kW high-power cabinets.

name: China Unicom Lianyungang Smart City Cloud Data Center
notes: Lianyun District disclosed an agreement for China Unicom Lianyungang to build a smart city cloud data center in the Lianyun New City big data industrial park for integrated services, application support, host hosting and related cloud services.

name: BDx NKG1 / Nanjing Data Center Campus
developer: BDx Data Centers / Nanjing Zihai Data
notes: BDx announced phase one of its 35 MW NKG campus live; NKG1 provides 4 MW IT power and is Tier III design certified, with grid approval for 60 MVA for the campus.

name: China Mobile Yangtze River Delta (Nanjing) Data Center
notes: Located in Nanjing Jiangbei New Area; public reports describe four data-center buildings and five support buildings, 18,000 to 19,000 cabinets, 300,000 servers, and long-term export bandwidth over 10T.

name: Alibaba Jiangsu Cloud Computing Data Center
notes: Originally signed in Nantong with RMB 18 billion investment, 450 mu site and planned 300,000 servers; DCD later reported Alibaba Cloud finished super data centers in Nantong, Hangzhou and Ulanqab. A 2020 expansion signing was reported at RMB 15 billion.

name: Princeton Digital Group NT1 Nantong
notes: PDG's China locations page lists Nantong NT1 as 64 MW across four buildings; third-party listing places it in the Nantong Economic and Technological Development Zone IDC park.

name: OneAsia Jiangsu Nantong Data Centre
notes: OneAsia describes the site as located in the Nantong International Data Centre Zone near Shanghai; DataCenterMap lists the strategic flagship Nantong facility as supported by 80 MW IT load.

name: JD Cloud East China Data Center
notes: Jiangsu party-news article says JD Cloud East China Data Center phase one had 150,000 servers in service in Suqian; hosting provider pages also identify Suqian JD Cloud data center services.

name: GLP Changshu Southeast Data Centre
notes: GLP announced first phase delivery of a Changshu, Jiangsu data center campus targeted for more than 120 MW IT capacity at full buildout and capacity for over 300,000 servers.

name: GDS Kunshan / Guojin Data Center
developer: GDS Holdings / Guojin Data Technology Development (Kunshan) Co.
notes: Kunshan government report says the Guojin data center in Huaqiao Economic Development Zone was invested and built by a GDS subsidiary, includes two data-center buildings, 4,192 cabinets and 29,044 kW designed power capacity, completed and operational in 2020.

name: China Mobile Jiangsu Suzhou Data Center
notes: Phase I had more than 5,000 cabinets; phase II started with about RMB 1.9 billion planned investment, 86,000 sqm construction area and about 11,000 additional cabinets. Jiangsu Mobile report refers to Suzhou Fenhu as a Huawei Cloud core node.

name: Chayora Greater Shanghai Data Centre Campus (Taicang)
notes: Chayora announced a Greater Shanghai campus serving the region; trade reporting says the campus, in Taicang near Shanghai, covers 8.5 acres, includes three five-story buildings, 54 MW capacity and 10,000 racks, with first facility completed before 2023 service readiness.

name: Suzhou International Science-Park Data Center
developer: Suzhou International Science-Park Data Center Co.
notes: Uptime Institute client profile says SISDC was backed by the Suzhou government and built by Suzhou Industrial Park as a public technology platform, providing customized IDC services.

name: Taizhou Intelligent Computing Center
developer: Taizhou Medical High-tech Zone / Gaogang District
notes: Jiangsu Cyberspace Administration article describes Taizhou Intelligent Computing Center as the city's largest and most advanced/reliable data center, designed to T3+ standard, able to host 50,000 servers and at least 40 PB storage, due to enter operation in H2 2022.

name: Zhihuifengcheng Data Center Phase I
notes: Operator page lists Taizhou Zhihuifengcheng Data Center phase I as Tier3+, 1,000 racks and 12,000 KVA total power.

name: Zhihuifengcheng Data Center Phase II
notes: Operator page lists Taizhou Zhihuifengcheng Data Center phase II as Tier3+ with 5,000 racks; total power not disclosed in accessible listing.

name: China Mobile Wuxi Taike Park Data Center
notes: Jiangsu Mobile report says the Wuxi Taike Park data center had all 8,000 cabinets in production, carrying China Mobile cloud and Huawei joint-cloud East China resource pools and serving customers including Baidu, China Merchants Bank and Wuxi public security.

name: China Telecom Wuxi Guomai IDC
notes: Data-center directory identifies China Telecom Wuxi Guomai IDC in Liangxi District, Wuxi; capacity details not disclosed.

name: Wuxi International Data Center
notes: Colocation provider page describes Wuxi International Data Center as a Tier 4-class facility with dual utility and UPS power and telecom/unicom/BGP bandwidth; treated as directory/provider evidence.

name: Xuzhou Public Security Bureau Data Centers
notes: Procurement notice for Xuzhou Public Security Bureau data center maintenance states existing data center computer rooms at three sites, two in Quanshan District and one in Yunlong District, covering machine-room facilities, network, big data, cloud computing and storage resources.

name: Xuzhou Yunlong District Court Data Center Machine Room Micro-module Upgrade
notes: Government procurement result for data center machine-room micro-module upgrade; awarded to Jiangsu Mobile Information System Integration for RMB 2.0368 million.

name: Xuzhou Data Resource Center / One Center Two Platforms
notes: Jiangsu party-news report says Xuzhou built a data-service system centered on a data resource center, big data sharing/exchange platform and public data open platform; physical data-center capacity not disclosed.

name: Yancheng Marine Intelligent Computing Center
developer: Yancheng Huanghai New Area / CSCEC Fourth Bureau contractor
notes: CSCEC reports official construction start in Huanghai New Area Binhai area, RMB 6 billion planned investment, about 60,000 sqm GFA, two data-center buildings, one 110kV energy station, one integrated building and 2,520 high-performance computing servers; target PUE 1.198.

name: Yancheng Municipal Government Information Resource Center Phase I
notes: Digital Yancheng white paper coverage says the city had built 8,800 sqm of machine rooms with 1,018 servers and 489 storage devices, and that the municipal government information resource center phase I came online at the end of 2015.
